hooks.text: Four interacting galaxies share the sky with a supersonic impostor.
A famous galaxy group hides an interloper plowing through at supersonic speeds.
One galaxy in Stephan's Quintet sits thirty-nine million light-years closer than the rest.

title: The Supersonic Interloper in Stephan's Quintet
description: Discover the shocking truth behind Stephan's Quintet, where a foreground galaxy crashes through the group at supersonic speeds.

beats.text: Four interacting galaxies share the sky with a supersonic impostor.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope mosaic of Stephan's Quintet, 2009

beats.text: Discovered in 1877 by Édouard Stephan, this group in Pegasus looks like a tight squad.
beats.visual: Pegasus constellation map showing Stephan's Quintet location

beats.text: Modern telescopes revealed that the brightest member, NGC 7320, is actually a foreground interloper.
beats.visual: James Webb Space Telescope NIRCam image of Stephan's Quintet, 2022
queries: Stephan's Quintet James Webb Space Telescope

beats.text: It sits just thirty-nine million light-years away, while the other four are parked much further out.
beats.visual: Galaxy redshift distance diagram for Hickson Compact Group 92

beats.text: Another intruder named NGC 7318B is currently plowing straight into the group.
beats.visual: Artist concept of supersonic galactic collision and bow shock
queries: Galaxy collision shock wave artist concept

beats.text: This supersonic impact generates a colossal shock wave bigger than the entire Milky Way.
emphasis: bigger than the entire Milky Way
beats.visual: Chandra X-ray Observatory composite of Stephan's Quintet shock wave, 2006

beats.text: Even Hollywood used the group to represent glowing angels in the holiday classic It's a Wonderful Life.
beats.visual: It's a Wonderful Life film frame featuring opening angel concept, 1946
queries: It's a Wonderful Life opening scene angels
